conviction_note: The evidence is balanced with a slight positive lean. The bar was cut hard after August, management named Q3 as its hardest quarter, JD's North American comps improved over the same weeks, the sporting-goods Census series held about +9% YoY, and the CFO bought $1m mid-quarter. Against that sit Nike's Jordan retro reduction (Williams Trading: a 40-50% allocation cut in FY27), Williams' weak back-to-school call for Foot Locker, and a name whose last two beat-and-raise prints went -4.8% and +0.2%. p_up is 52 on an 11% abs move (+0.44); the findings sum to +0.80. The gap is small and comes from the reaction function: this stock does not pay for reported-quarter beats, so the guide carries the sign.
bar: Q3 FY26 EPS consensus $1.38 (Zacks, via Earnings Whispers/Finviz preview 2026-11-16, https://finviz.com/news/423376/dicks-faces-margin-trough-test-as-foot-locker-drag-tests-core-strength; whisper $1.46) and $1.42 (Fiscal.ai, via Stocktwits 2026-11-19, https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/dks-stock-gets-a-sell-rating-ahead-of-q3-earnings-analyst-warns-fy-27-outlook-about-to-get-worse/cNbiWEAR90W). Revenue $5.06-5.08B. Last year Q3 EPS $2.78. Company FY26 guide (2026-08-25 release, https://s205.q4cdn.com/510074553/files/doc_news/DICKS-Sporting-Goods-Inc--Reports-Second-Quarter-Results-2026.pdf): non-GAAP EPS $11.00-12.00 (H1 was $6.43, so H2 implied $4.57-5.57), net sales $21.9-22.2B, DICK'S comps +2.5% to +4.0%, Foot Locker proforma comps -2% to 0%, Foot Locker segment loss $40-80M. Two estimate sources roughly agree, so the bar is usable. print_vs_bar_pct is measured on EPS against $1.40.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 6.2M shares at the 2026-08-14 settlement, 4.2 days to cover (aggregator snippet; https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DKS/short-interest and https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/DKS/short-interest both returned 403). MarketBeat had 8.98% of float at 2026-04-30. That is not a crowded short. Skew is +1.66 vol points with put/call OI 1.54, a mildly downside-paying, broadly balanced market. The event-implied move is 11.05% (straddle 12.0%). The stock is -8.3% over 5 days, -6.7% over 20 days and -43.7% from its 52-week high. Part of the 5-day fall is the Williams Trading Sell downgrade of 2026-11-19 (DKS -5% intraday per TIKR).

findings.finding: JD Sports, the closest North American comparable to Foot Locker (JD/Finish Line/Shoe Palace), reported North America LFL of -2.2% for the 13 weeks to 31 Oct 2026, against -6.8% in the prior quarter. That window is almost the same as DKS's Q3 (2 Aug-31 Oct). JD credited back-to-school demand shifting into the period. It also said footwear stayed under pressure from end-of-cycle lines and promotions, and cut the top of its FY profit range from £800m to £750m. Foot Locker's Q2 proforma comp was -3.6% and its FY guide is -2% to 0%, which implies H2 between about -2.4% and +1.4%. A sequential improvement like JD's would put Foot Locker inside or above that guide on sales, while promotions still weigh on margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Foot Locker comps were the line that broke in August 2026 (-3.6% against +0.6% the quarter before), alongside the guide cut, and the stock fell -30.7%. No print yet where Foot Locker comps surprised upward.
findings.why_not_priced: JD is a UK-listed name, and US previews (Earnings Whispers 11-16, Williams 11-19) do not cite it. Williams calls Foot Locker back-to-school traffic weak. If the market had taken the JD read, the stock would not have fallen 8% in the five days into the print on a Foot Locker-traffic downgrade.
findings.independence: Partial support from the Census sporting-goods series (separate finding, different source). The Williams Trading note argues the opposite for Foot Locker's back-to-school traffic. The margin caveat comes from the same JD document and is netted into this size.

findings.finding: Census advance retail sales for sporting goods/hobby/music/book stores (FRED RSSGHBMS, seasonally adjusted) for Aug-Oct 2026 total $26.13B against $23.95B for Aug-Oct 2025, +9.1% YoY (Aug +9.5%, Sep +10.9%, Oct +7.1%). That matches July 2026's +9.0% YoY, so the category did not slow into DKS's Q3. October was down about 0.7% m/m. This points to the core DICK'S business holding its +2.5% to +4.0% comp guide; Q2 core comp was +4.9%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Core comp beats have not paid on this name. Aug 2025 (beat and raise) -4.84%, Nov 2025 +0.2%, Aug 2026 core +4.9% swamped by the guide cut.
findings.why_not_priced: The core business is already seen as the healthy part, so this is largely expected. It matters only against a bear case that core slowed in Q3, which the series does not support.
findings.independence: Broad proxy, not company-level. JD's improvement (separate source) points the same way for footwear specialty.

findings.finding: Insiders bought after the Q2 collapse and, in two cases, mid-way through Q3. CFO Navdeep Gupta bought 7,707 shares ($1.0M at $129.75) on 2026-09-22. Foot Locker International President Matthew Barnes bought 3,665 shares ($0.5M at $136.39) on 2026-09-30. Directors bought about $3.7M on 26-27 Aug (Barrenechea $2.2M, Colombo, Mathrani, Eddy) and Fitzgerald $0.24M on 23 Sep. The CFO had seven weeks of Q3 data when he bought, 20 days after reaffirming nothing intra-quarter. That is hard to square with a second guide cut he could already see.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance in the baseline of a CFO open-market buy before a print. The August 2026 guide cut cost -30.7%, so the guide line is the one this stock moves on.
findings.why_not_priced: The Form 4s are public, but the stock is back near the CFO's purchase price ($134.78 against $129.75). Previews discuss Williams' 'miss or low end' risk without weighing the CFO's mid-quarter buy. If priced, the downgrade would not have taken 5% off.
findings.independence: https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Foot+Locker+President+Buys+%24500%2C000+of+DICK%27S+Sporting+Goods+Stock (2026-10-02) confirms the Barnes buy and the CFO buy. Same underlying Form 4 data.

findings.finding: Nike said on its Q1 FY27 call (2026-10-01) that it will deliberately reduce the volume and frequency of specific Jordan retro launches after talking with wholesale partners, with North America feeling the biggest near-term impact. Williams Trading (2026-11-19) estimates Jordan allocation cuts to DKS/Foot Locker of 15-20% in Q1 FY27 and 40-50% for FY27. It puts Jordan at about 25% of Foot Locker's US revenue, a roughly $500M headwind of which only about half can be offset. Management will be asked on the call, and Q4 launch-calendar or early FY27 commentary could disappoint.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In August 2026 Foot Locker launches 'performed below industry and our expectations' and that drove the cut and the -30.7% move. Launch and allocation news on Foot Locker has been the name's most violent line.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: DKS fell about 5% on the note and is -8.3% over 5 days. The size is held below the implied move for that reason. The unpriced part is whether management confirms a FY27 allocation cut of that size on the call; Nike's own wording gave no number.
findings.independence: Nike's own statement: https://about.nike.com/en/newsroom/releases/nike-inc-reports-fiscal-2027-first-quarter-results (2026-10-01, release says 'deliberate actions' on Jordan; the retro reduction quote is from the call). Both are the same underlying fact, merged here.

findings.finding: Williams Trading (Sam Poser, downgrade to Sell, PT $120, 2026-11-19) expects weak back-to-school traffic and elevated Foot Locker inventory to put DKS at risk of missing its FY26 guide or landing at the low end ($11.00 non-GAAP EPS).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide cut in August 2026 moved the stock -30.7%. A second cut or a move to the low end would land on the same line.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the note is in the wire copy and moved the stock. This is sell-side inference, not a company number, and JD's same-period North America improvement argues against the weak back-to-school claim. Hence the small size.
findings.independence: Same document as the Jordan quantification in the previous finding; this is a separate claim (FY26 traffic and inventory, not FY27 allocation). Contradicted in direction by JD's North America LFL improvement (https://fashionunited.com/news/business/jd-sports-narrows-fy27-profit-outlook-as-third-quarter-footwear-demand-remains-soft/2026111975844).

findings.finding: Management pre-set Q3 as the trough on the Q2 call. Gross-margin pressure would be 'most pronounced in Q3', with nearly 50bp of SG&A deleverage in Q3 at the midpoint, and Ed Stack said 'Q3 is going to be a bit more difficult than Q4'. Consensus EPS is $1.38-1.42 against $2.78 a year ago. A reported quarter that merely lands at the guided trough is inside the guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reported-quarter beats on DKS have been sold or ignored (2025-03 -5.7%, 2025-08 -4.8%, 2025-11 +0.2%).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the company told the market, so this sits inside guidance and is sized near zero. The residual is that a low, explicitly guided bar makes a headline EPS miss less likely.
findings.independence: The Earnings Whispers/Finviz preview (https://finviz.com/news/423376/dicks-faces-margin-trough-test-as-foot-locker-drag-tests-core-strength, 2026-11-16) restates the 'low point for margins' framing.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is washed out relative to the guide. The stock is $134.78, -8.3% in 5 days, -43.7% from its 52-week high and about 11% above its 52-week low. The whisper is $1.46 against $1.38-1.42 consensus. Wells Fargo raised its PT to $195 on 2026-11-13, expecting Q3 above lowered expectations. Short interest is modest (about 4 days to cover), so no squeeze mechanism either way.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the -30.7% gap in August the stock held $120-150 for three months, with insider buying at about $129.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. It is filed because the five-day decline into the print is a downgrade-driven move rather than new company data.

findings.finding: DKS received about $59M of IEEPA tariff refunds in Q2 ($57M DICK'S, $2M Foot Locker). About $21M was included in non-GAAP and $38M excluded as prior-year. Management said it reinvested the refunds into pricing to offset promotion. Further refunds could land in Q3 (no company statement on Q3 timing).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 the refunds landed and the stock fell -30.7% on the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly excluded from non-GAAP and reinvested in price, so it has no stated path to the guide. Hence the token size.
findings.independence: Q2 call summary (https://www.webull.com/news/15463631008252928) gives the same split; same company source.

outside_window.finding: FY27 Jordan allocation cuts of 40-50% (Williams Trading estimate) would hit FY27 sales from February 2027. The formal FY27 guide comes with the Q4 print in March 2027.

rejected_candidates.detail: Dated 2025-11-21. It describes the prior-year Q3, not this print.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Earnings Whispers preview claim that FY consensus is $14.24 (above the $11-12 guide), implying stale estimates
rejected_candidates.detail: The article itself says the figure likely predates the August cut. Q3 consensus at $1.38-1.42 shows estimates were cut, so it is not evidence of a stale bar.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Academy Sports Q2 FY26 (2026-09-09): comps -0.4%, FY comp guide trimmed to 0-2% at midpoint, EPS guide raised, lower-income consumer pressured
rejected_candidates.detail: Its quarter ended 1 Aug (DKS's Q2, already reported). The read for Aug-Oct is covered by the Census series and JD findings; the signal is mixed and weak.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Fox/regional reports that DKS plans to close Foot Locker stores with $500-750M of charges
rejected_candidates.detail: A November 2025 story; the Q2 2026 release shows 84 North America Foot Locker-banner closures year to date already disclosed, so it is not new.

baseline_tension: Mild positive lean against a mildly positive (downside-paying) skew of +1.66 and a -8.3% five-day run-in. The skew is small, so there is little to beat. The lean rests on the run-in being a sell-side downgrade rather than company data, and the p_up is held near 50 because this name sells beats and the Jordan overhang is real.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; DKS sold its 2025 beat-and-raise prints): JD North America read cut from +1.0 to +0.7 and the Census series from +0.8 to +0.5; p_up 53 -> 52.
Rule 5 (documents beat inference): the insider-buying finding is a Form 4 fact but an inference about the guide, so cut from +1.5 to +1.0.
Rule 2 (one-offs as one-offs): tariff refund cut from +0.2 to +0.1, since management says refunds are reinvested in price and mostly excluded from non-GAAP.

Rules 6, 7 and 9 left everything standing: the bar has two roughly agreeing sources plus a company guide, short interest is not crowded and the skew is small, and the Foot Locker findings are already sized net of the core business.
